cat > docker/recyclarr/recyclarr.yml <<'EOF'
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://schemas.recyclarr.dev/v8/config-schema.json
---
# Recyclarr configuration for Radarr and Sonarr. See docs/recyclarr.md for how
# this is deployed, previewed and synced.
#
# Profiles are guide-backed: each references a TRaSH Guides quality profile by
# trash_id, so qualities, cutoff, scores and the guide's default custom format
# groups (Unwanted Formats, Golden Rule HD, Streaming Services) come from the
# guide. Only deliberate deviations are written here as overrides. The "(Dual
# Audio)" profiles are named variants of the same guide profile.
#
# reset_unmatched_scores makes this file authoritative: a score set in the UI
# for a format not listed here is reset to 0 on the next sync.
#
# Two custom formats are bespoke (not published by TRaSH Guides) and are
# supplied from custom-formats/ via the resource providers in settings.yml.

radarr:
  radarr:
    base_url: http://radarr:7878
    api_key: !env_var RADARR_API_KEY

    # Streaming-service formats that score 0 are kept because the file naming
    # format prints matched custom formats (e.g. "[AMZN]"); never delete.
    delete_old_custom_formats: false

    quality_definition:
      type: movie

    media_management:
      propers_and_repacks: do_not_prefer

    quality_profiles:
      # TRaSH "WEB 1080p": WEB 1080p only, cutoff WEB 1080p, language Original,
      # upgrade until custom format score 10000. Used by English-original
      # movies (169 at the time of writing).
      - trash_id: e8c5acb741363a0dbda67d3978f4912f # WEB 1080p
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true

      # Variant for non-English movies. Bluray-1080p is merged into the 1080p
      # cutoff group so it ranks equal to WEB 1080p: Radarr only compares
      # custom format scores between equally ranked qualities, so a dual-audio
      # Bluray can replace an original-only WEB file (and vice versa) without
      # Bluray ever counting as a plain quality upgrade or downgrade.
      - trash_id: e8c5acb741363a0dbda67d3978f4912f # WEB 1080p
        name: WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: true
          until_quality: Bluray + WEB 1080p
          until_score: 10000
        qualities:
          - name: Bluray + WEB 1080p
            qualities:
              - Bluray-1080p
              - WEBDL-1080p
              - WEBRip-1080p
          - name: WEB 720p
            enabled: false
            qualities:
              - WEBDL-720p
              - WEBRip-720p
          - name: WEB 480p
            enabled: false
            qualities:
              - WEBDL-480p
              - WEBRip-480p
          - name: Remux-1080p
            enabled: false

      # Stock catch-all profile (6 movies). Upgrades disabled; only the
      # language guards are scored on it.
      - name: Any
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: false
        min_format_score: 0

    custom_format_groups:
      add:
        # Guide default groups for WEB 1080p (Unwanted Formats, Golden Rule
        # HD, Streaming Services General) sync automatically. The language
        # group is opt-in; select only "Wrong Language".
        - trash_id: 13856622cf7a6c9925d3a83f8812d679 # [Optional] Language Profiles
          select:
            - 2051402ee9ca81162017d98cbe1dff2c # Wrong Language
          assign_scores_to:
            - trash_id: e8c5acb741363a0dbda67d3978f4912f # WEB 1080p (both variants)
            - name: Any

    custom_formats:
      # Bespoke formats (see custom-formats/radarr and settings.yml). No guide
      # default exists, so the score is explicit.
      - trash_ids:
          - local-dual-audio-release-title-radarr # Dual Audio (Release Title)
        score: 2000
        assign_scores_to:
          - trash_id: e8c5acb741363a0dbda67d3978f4912f # WEB 1080p (both variants)
          - name: Any

      # Only on the Dual Audio variant: on an English-original movie this
      # format would reward releases bundling foreign dubs.
      - trash_ids:
          - local-dual-audio-original-english-radarr # Dual Audio (Original + English)
        score: 2000
        assign_scores_to:
          - name: WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)

    # media_naming intentionally omitted: the live naming formats don't match
    # any TRaSH Guides preset and syncing would rename the whole library.

sonarr:
  sonarr:
    base_url: http://sonarr:8989
    api_key: !env_var SONARR_API_KEY

    delete_old_custom_formats: false

    quality_definition:
      type: series

    media_management:
      propers_and_repacks: do_not_prefer

    quality_profiles:
      # TRaSH "WEB-1080p" for English-original series (61 at the time of
      # writing). The guide profile allows WEB 1080p only; the qualities
      # override keeps the previous guide's fallbacks (Bluray-1080p,
      # HDTV-1080p, 720p) allowed because 177 existing episode files use them
      # and disallowing them would queue all of those for re-download. Remove
      # the `qualities:` block to adopt the pure guide profile.
      - trash_id: 72dae194fc92bf828f32cde7744e51a1 # WEB-1080p
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        qualities:
          - name: WEB 1080p
            qualities:
              - WEBRip-1080p
              - WEBDL-1080p
          - name: Bluray-1080p
          - name: HDTV-1080p
          - name: WEB 720p
            qualities:
              - WEBRip-720p
              - WEBDL-720p
          - name: Bluray-720p
          - name: HDTV-720p

      # Variant for anime and other non-English series. Bluray-1080p is
      # merged into the cutoff group (same reasoning as the Radarr variant).
      - trash_id: 72dae194fc92bf828f32cde7744e51a1 # WEB-1080p
        name: WEB-1080p (Dual Audio)
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: true
          until_quality: Bluray + WEB 1080p
          until_score: 10000
        qualities:
          - name: Bluray + WEB 1080p
            qualities:
              - Bluray-1080p
              - WEBRip-1080p
              - WEBDL-1080p
          - name: HDTV-1080p
          - name: WEB 720p
            qualities:
              - WEBRip-720p
              - WEBDL-720p
          - name: Bluray-720p
          - name: HDTV-720p

      # Stock profiles still assigned to a few series. Upgrades disabled; only
      # the language guards (and, on the non-English ones, the dual-audio
      # bonus) are scored.
      - name: Any
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: false
      - name: Any (Dual Audio)
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: false
      - name: HD-1080p
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: false
      - name: HD - 720p/1080p
        reset_unmatched_scores:
          enabled: true
        upgrade:
          allowed: false

    custom_format_groups:
      add:
        # The language group is a guide default for WEB-1080p and would add
        # "Language: Not Original", which duplicates "Wrong Language". Keep
        # the single format and extend it to the stock profiles.
        - trash_id: 74aff4168620ed49dcc67e92b2c2a5b4 # [Optional] Language Profiles
          exclude:
            - ae575f95ab639ba5d15f663bf019e3e8 # Language: Not Original
          select:
            - 1fb6283bd05ab5c6a728cb213e5d07d8 # Wrong Language
          assign_scores_to:
            - trash_id: 72dae194fc92bf828f32cde7744e51a1 # WEB-1080p (both variants)
            - name: Any
            - name: Any (Dual Audio)
            - name: HD-1080p
            - name: HD - 720p/1080p

    custom_formats:
      - trash_ids:
          - local-dual-audio-release-title-sonarr # Dual Audio (Release Title)
        score: 2000
        assign_scores_to:
          - trash_id: 72dae194fc92bf828f32cde7744e51a1 # WEB-1080p (both variants)
          - name: Any
          - name: Any (Dual Audio)
          - name: HD-1080p
          - name: HD - 720p/1080p

      # Only on profiles holding non-English series (see the Radarr note).
      - trash_ids:
          - local-dual-audio-original-english-sonarr # Dual Audio (Original + English)
        score: 2000
        assign_scores_to:
          - name: WEB-1080p (Dual Audio)
          - name: Any (Dual Audio)
          - name: HD-1080p
          - name: HD - 720p/1080p

    # media_naming intentionally omitted (see the Radarr note).
EOF

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/recyclarr.md'; s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('## What Recyclarr manages'); end=s.index('## Deployment')
new="""## What Recyclarr manages

- **Quality profiles** are guide-backed: `recyclarr.yml` references the TRaSH
  Guides profile by `trash_id` (Radarr `WEB 1080p`, Sonarr `WEB-1080p`) and
  Recyclarr pulls the quality order, cutoff, upgrade settings, scores and the
  guide's default custom format groups (Unwanted Formats, Golden Rule HD,
  Streaming Services) from the guide. Only deliberate deviations are written as
  overrides:
  - `WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)` / `WEB-1080p (Dual Audio)` are named variants of
    the same guide profile for non-English titles. Bluray-1080p is merged into
    the 1080p cutoff group so it ranks equal to WEB 1080p; Radarr and Sonarr
    only compare custom format scores between equally ranked qualities, so a
    dual-audio Bluray can replace an original-only WEB file without Bluray
    ever counting as a plain quality upgrade or downgrade.
  - Sonarr `WEB-1080p` keeps the previous guide's fallback qualities
    (Bluray-1080p, HDTV-1080p, 720p) allowed because 177 existing episode
    files use them. Remove that `qualities:` block to adopt the pure guide
    profile; Sonarr will then queue those episodes for upgrade.
  - The stock `Any`, `Any (Dual Audio)`, `HD-1080p` and `HD - 720p/1080p`
    profiles carry only the language guards and the dual-audio bonus.
- **Scores are authoritative.** `reset_unmatched_scores` is enabled on every
  managed profile, so a score set in the UI for a format that is not in
  `recyclarr.yml` is reset to 0 on the next sync.
- **Custom formats** come from the guide's groups plus the `Wrong Language`
  format from the language group (the group's default `Language: Not Original`
  is excluded because it duplicates it). Two bespoke formats,
  `Dual Audio (Original + English)` and `Dual Audio (Release Title)`, are not
  published by TRaSH Guides; their specifications live in
  `docker/recyclarr/custom-formats/{radarr,sonarr}/*.json` and are registered
  as local `resource_providers` in `docker/recyclarr/settings.yml`, so they are
  referenced by a `local-...` trash ID like any guide format.
- **Quality definitions** follow the guide's `movie` and `series` size tables.
  At adoption these matched the live values (the guide's current maximums are
  effectively unlimited).

## What stays manual

- **Media naming**: the live naming formats don't match any TRaSH Guides
  preset and syncing them would rename the whole library. `media_naming` is
  left out so Recyclarr never touches it.
- **Radarr quality profile language** (`Original` on the two WEB 1080p
  profiles) is synced from the guide profile; the stock `Any` profile's
  language stays manual. Language preference is otherwise expressed through
  the custom formats above.
- **Delay profiles, indexers, download clients, and root folders** are
  entirely outside Recyclarr's scope and stay manual in Radarr/Sonarr/Prowlarr.
- **Lidarr** is not supported by Recyclarr at all (confirmed against upstream
  docs — Recyclarr only targets Radarr and Sonarr). Lidarr custom formats and
  quality profiles remain fully manual.
- **Unscored streaming-service formats** in Radarr (AMZN, NF, ...) exist only
  so the file naming format can print them; `delete_old_custom_formats` stays
  `false` so Recyclarr never removes them.

"""
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
start=s.index('## First-sync caution')
s=s[:start]+"""## First-sync caution

The first sync takes ownership of the profiles and custom formats above.
Preview it first (`sync --preview`, with `--log debug` to see the per-format
diff; Recyclarr 8 reports only a summary at the default level). When this
stack was introduced the preview showed:

- Radarr: four new unwanted formats scored -10000 on both 1080p profiles (Bad
  Dual Groups, Black and White Editions, Line/Mic Dubbed, Upscaled). No quality,
  cutoff or size changes.
- Sonarr: the same two unwanted formats that exist for series (Bad Dual Groups,
  Upscaled), streaming-service scores moved from the old guide's tiered values
  to the current flat 75, three new streaming formats (ATV, PLAY, ROKU) and the
  HD/UHD Streaming Boost formats at 75, and the `Bluray + WEB 1080p` group
  created on the Dual Audio profile.

Both servers' `Repack v2`/`Repack v3` and Radarr's `Remux + WEB 1080p`
profiles were renamed to the guide names (`Repack2`/`Repack3`, `WEB 1080p`)
before adoption so Recyclarr updates them in place instead of creating
duplicates. `delete_old_custom_formats: false` means nothing is ever deleted;
formats not listed here are left untouched apart from their score being reset
to 0 on managed profiles.
"""
open(p,'w').write(s); print('doc updated')
EOF
grep -c '' docs/recyclarr.md

content.text:
All approved optimisations are applied, verified with a read-only preview, and still uncommitted for your inspection.

**What changed in the repo**

- `docker/recyclarr/recyclarr.yml` is now 240 lines instead of about 800. Both apps use guide-backed profiles: TRaSH "WEB 1080p" for Radarr and "WEB-1080p" for Sonarr, with the Dual Audio profiles as named variants of the same id. Only your deviations are written as overrides.
- `reset_unmatched_scores` is on for every managed profile, so git is authoritative for scores.
- Quality definitions follow the guide's movie and series tables. The preview confirmed they already match live.
- Sonarr streaming scores drop their explicit overrides and take the guide's flat 75.
- The two local Repack JSON files are gone. The schema header line is in. Compose has a read-only root filesystem with a tmpfs, and the preview ran successfully under exactly those flags.
- `docs/recyclarr.md` rewritten to describe the guide-backed model and the expected first-sync diff.

**One-off live changes I made to enable this**

- Sonarr custom formats renamed "Repack v2/v3" to "Repack2/Repack3".
- Radarr profiles renamed to "WEB 1080p" and "WEB 1080p (Dual Audio)", since Remux is no longer wanted and the guide profile carries that name.

**Two judgement calls to be aware of**

- Sonarr's live WEB-1080p allows the old guide's fallbacks (Bluray, HDTV, 720p) and 177 episode files use them. I kept those allowed via an override so nothing gets queued for re-download. Deleting that one `qualities:` block adopts the pure guide profile.
- I applied the same Bluray + WEB equal-rank group to the Sonarr Dual Audio variant for consistency with Radarr. Anime Blurays are the common dual-audio source, so this is where it pays off. Recyclarr will create that group on first sync.

**What the first sync will do**, verified from the debug-level preview:

| App | Change |
|---|---|
| Radarr | Adds Bad Dual Groups, Black and White Editions, Line/Mic Dubbed, Upscaled at -10000 on both 1080p profiles. Nothing else. |
| Sonarr | Adds Bad Dual Groups and Upscaled at -10000. Streaming scores to 75, plus ATV, PLAY, ROKU and the HD/UHD Streaming Boost formats at 75. Creates the Bluray + WEB 1080p group on the Dual Audio profile. |

Both servers' profiles were byte-identical before and after the preview, so it wrote nothing. A note for the doc and for you: Recyclarr 8 reports config validation errors only at debug level, which is why two of my intermediate runs looked like silent no-ops. The doc now says to preview with `--log debug`.

**Check result**

The final preview's debug log was clean: no errors, no validation failures. The only warning was the expected notice that Recyclarr is taking over the four guide-backed profiles, and the one "not found" line was the intended creation of the Sonarr Bluray + WEB group.

**What is live**

- The first real sync ran against Radarr and Sonarr from the host. The before/after diff matched the preview exactly: 7 new formats per app, guide-content refreshes on 13 Radarr and 10 Sonarr formats, Sonarr streaming scores to 75, and the new Bluray + WEB 1080p group and cutoff on the Sonarr Dual Audio profile. Nothing deleted, profile language still Original, dual-audio files still score 2000.
- One effect not in the preview summary: the Remux Tier scores dropped to 0 on both Radarr profiles because the guide's WEB 1080p profile doesn't carry them. Remux isn't an allowed quality, so this has no practical effect.
- PR #1717 passed the docker render check and is squash-merged to main as a4cab4a0. Local main is up to date and clean.

**One step only you can do**

Create the `recyclarr` Git stack in Portainer pointing at `docker/recyclarr/compose.yml`, set `TZ`, `RADARR_API_KEY` and `SONARR_API_KEY` on the stack, and turn on "Enable relative path volumes". Until then the config is applied but not yet re-synced daily.

45 Remux-1080p movie files sit below the WEB 1080p cutoff on both Radarr profiles, and have since before today. Radarr will replace them with WEB-DLs whenever those movies are searched, as happened with Hotarubi earlier. If you'd rather keep the remuxes, re-enabling Remux-1080p on the profiles is a two-line override in recyclarr.yml.

# Git Repository Deployment Configuration

## Enable Relative Path Volumes

The documentation states: "When you toggle **Enable relative path volumes** to on, you are able to specify relative path references in your compose files."

A key limitation is noted: "This feature is only available in Portainer Business Edition."

The documentation does not mention whether this setting can be toggled after initial stack creation or how GitOps updates interact with this feature.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

occ() {

}

  echo "The NFS data directory is missing at /var/www/html/data" >&2

occ background:cron

  occ app:enable twofactor_totp
fi
occ richdocuments:activate-config \
  --wopi-url=http://nextcloud-office:9980 \
  --callback-url=http://nextcloud

        while read -r script_file_path; do

volume that does not exist on the host. Docker created an empty directory in
its place and the hook could never run. Ship the script as an inline compose
config with an executable mode instead, which needs no host path.

content.text:
All three final downloads imported with the right audio, so everything from this round is closed out.

**Verified imports**

| Title | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Prix of Europe | English only | German + English, dual-audio score 2000 |
| Descendants: Wicked World S01E03 | Hebrew only | Disney+ multi-language incl. English |
| Chuck S03E06 | Italian only | English + Portuguese |

**CI resolved repo-wide**

- Root cause: the September 6 RouterOS commit added two "Proxmox -> TrueNAS NFS" forward rules without updating the policy test, and the path-scoped ansible workflow never ran on that commit. Fixed in #1719 (test passes locally and in CI, ansible-lint clean).
- All three open Renovate PRs (#1712, #1713, #1716) rebased and are green. They are collection bumps, so they await your approval as before.

**Other fixes landed today**

- Nextcloud's post-install hook is now an inline compose config with executable mode (#1719). Portainer already redeployed it and the container shows a real 591-byte executable where the empty directory was.
- `/srv/portainer` is created by the docker-host role and documented (#1718).
- YAML custom tags declared for the editor (#1722), which clears the "Unresolved tag" error.
- SABnzbd smart-duplicate handling is on Tag (your change). I cleared 23 stale Grand Prix blocklist entries it had caused, plus today's Sonarr ones.

The last remaining note is the Recyclarr Portainer stack itself, which needs you to create it with `TZ`, `RADARR_API_KEY`, `SONARR_API_KEY`, relative path volumes on, and `/srv/portainer` as the local filesystem path. Until then the synced config is live but not re-applied daily.

input.description: Audit Jellyfin metadata matches
input.prompt:
Read-only audit of a Jellyfin media server's metadata matching. Do NOT modify anything in Jellyfin (GET requests only), do not delete or move files, do not restart containers.

Access: `ssh mm@docker-host 'cmd'`. Containers: `jellyfin` (port 8096 inside the container, on the Docker network `proxy`; library bind-mounted at /data/media from host /mnt/data/media, music at /data/music), `radarr` (7878), `sonarr` (8989), `pinchflat` (YouTube downloader writing to /downloads = host /mnt/data/media/youtube), `jellyplex-watched`. Ports are NOT published on the host. The Jellyfin API token is available as the `JELLYFIN_TOKEN` environment variable of the `jellyplex-watched` container: `ssh mm@docker-host "docker inspect jellyplex-watched --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' | grep -i JELLYFIN"` (also note JELLYFIN_BASEURL). Call the API from inside the jellyfin container: `docker exec jellyfin curl -s -H 'Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=TOKEN' 'http://127.0.0.1:8096/...'` (if curl is missing there, use `docker run --rm --network proxy curlimages/curl:8.10.1 -s ... http://jellyfin:8096/...`). Radarr/Sonarr API keys: `docker exec radarr sed -n 's:.*<ApiKey>\(.*\)</ApiKey>.*:\1:p' /config/config.xml` (same for sonarr); call them via `docker exec radarr curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: KEY' http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/...`. Host has jq and python3. Save large JSON in your scratchpad /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/d3f24245-e5fb-4811-8dbe-b9304620c838/scratchpad with a `jf_` prefix and analyse with python3. Never write tokens into the repo; redact them in your report.

GOAL: find every Jellyfin item whose metadata match is wrong or missing, across all libraries (Movies, TV, YouTube, and anything else configured), and gather what is needed to fix each one.

Steps:
1. `GET /System/Info` (version), `GET /Library/VirtualFolders` (libraries: name, type, paths, and the library options: metadata fetchers/savers enabled, PreferredMetadataLanguage, whether "Enable real time monitoring", automatic refresh, chapter image extraction, and the TypeOptions with their MetadataFetchers/ImageFetchers order). Note which libraries are Movies/Shows/Mixed/Music and which folder each maps to.
2. Movies: `GET /Items?IncludeItemTypes=Movie&Recursive=true&Fields=Path,ProviderIds,ProductionYear,OriginalTitle,Overview,DateCreated,MediaSources&userId=<any admin user id from GET /Users>` (page if needed). For each movie: Jellyfin Name, ProductionYear, ProviderIds (Tmdb/Imdb), Path. The Radarr folder naming embeds the intended ID: `{tmdb-XXXX}` in the folder name. Flag a MISMATCH when the folder's tmdb id ≠ Jellyfin's Tmdb provider id, or when Jellyfin's year/title obviously differs from the folder (e.g. "The Jungle Book (2016) {tmdb-278927}" matched to the 1967 cartoon). Also flag: missing ProviderIds (unidentified), missing Overview/no poster (check `ImageTags`), items whose Path does not exist under /data/media/movies (orphans), and movies present on disk / in Radarr but absent from Jellyfin (compare with Radarr `GET /api/v3/movie` hasFile paths translated from /data/media/movies ... same mount name inside jellyfin: /data/media/movies). Also detect duplicate movies (two Jellyfin items for the same tmdb id or same folder).
3. TV: `GET /Items?IncludeItemTypes=Series&Recursive=true&Fields=Path,ProviderIds,ProductionYear,Overview` — Sonarr folder naming embeds `{tvdb-XXXX}`. Flag mismatches between folder tvdb id and Jellyfin Tvdb provider id, unidentified series, series on disk/in Sonarr missing from Jellyfin. Then episodes: `GET /Items?IncludeItemTypes=Episode&Recursive=true&Fields=Path,ParentIndexNumber,IndexNumber,ProviderIds` — flag episodes with missing season/episode numbers, episodes whose file name S##E## disagrees with Jellyfin's ParentIndexNumber/IndexNumber, "virtual"/missing episodes vs files present, and episode files on disk (from Sonarr `GET /api/v3/episodefile?seriesId=` for each series, or a `find /data/media/tv -type f` inside the container) that Jellyfin has not indexed. Specifically report the state of the series "Sterling Point" (any files, which episodes exist, whether episode 2 is present in Sonarr and Jellyfin).
4. YouTube: identify how the youtube folder is structured (`docker exec jellyfin find /data/media/youtube -maxdepth 3 | head -50`, count files, presence of .nfo/.jpg sidecars from Pinchflat) and which Jellyfin library covers it and with what content type and metadata settings. Report how the items appear (as Series/Season/Episode? as Movies? as Videos?), whether channels are matched to wrong TV shows (a channel folder mis-identified as a TV series by TVDB is a classic problem), items with no metadata, and duplicates. Check Pinchflat's settings if accessible (its config DB or UI settings are in the pinchflat-data volume: look for the media profile output path template and whether NFO/thumbnail generation is on) — read-only.
5. Check Jellyfin logs for metadata/probe problems: `docker exec jellyfin sh -c 'ls -t /config/log | head -3'` then grep the latest 2 logs for "Error", "ffprobe", "Failed", "could not be found", "Unable to" and summarise recurring items (file paths). Redact tokens.

REPORT (final message only): Jellyfin version; library table (name, type, path, fetcher order, key options); MOVIES mismatch table (Jellyfin ItemId | Jellyfin name/year/TmdbId | folder | folder tmdb id | problem); TV mismatch table (series ItemId | name | TvdbId vs folder | problem) and episode-level problems; YouTube findings; orphan/duplicate/missing lists; log findings; and for each fix the exact API fields I would need (ItemId, correct provider id). Keep it compact; if a list is long, give the count and the first 20 with the full list saved to a scratchpad file (state the path).

input.description: Audit media file integrity
input.prompt:
Read-only integrity audit of a media library. Do NOT delete, move, rename or modify any file; do not change Radarr/Sonarr (GET only); do not restart containers. Be considerate of the host: it is a live media server on NFS storage, so limit ffprobe concurrency to about 4 parallel processes and do NOT fully decode files (no `ffmpeg -f null` over whole files).

Access: `ssh mm@docker-host 'cmd'`. Library on the host: /mnt/data/media/{movies,tv,youtube,...} (NFS). The `jellyfin` container mounts it at /data/media and has ffprobe at /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe (use `docker exec jellyfin /usr/lib/jellyfin-ffmpeg/ffprobe ...`). Radarr (7878) and Sonarr (8989) containers mount it at /data/media as well; their API keys: `docker exec radarr sed -n 's:.*<ApiKey>\(.*\)</ApiKey>.*:\1:p' /config/config.xml` (same for sonarr); call `docker exec radarr curl -s -H 'X-Api-Key: KEY' http://127.0.0.1:7878/api/v3/...`. Host has jq, python3. Scratchpad for your files: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/d3f24245-e5fb-4811-8dbe-b9304620c838/scratchpad (prefix `integ_`). Note: Radarr is currently downloading replacements for ~30 movies (Remux files being replaced by WEB-DL); files under /data/media/movies may change while you scan — record timestamps and don't treat a just-replaced file as an anomaly. Redact API keys in your report.

GOAL: find broken, truncated, corrupt, zero-length, or otherwise unplayable media files, plus files the download managers don't know about (orphans) and library entries whose files are missing, across movies, TV and YouTube. The user reports that "Sterling Point" episode 2 was corrupt (they may have deleted it since).

Method:
1. Inventory: `docker exec jellyfin find /data/media -type f \( -iname '*.mkv' -o -iname '*.mp4' -o -iname '*.avi' -o -iname '*.m4v' -o -iname '*.webm' -o -iname '*.ts' -o -iname '*.mov' \) -printf '%s\t%TY-%Tm-%Td\t%p\n'` → save the list; counts per top-level folder; total size. Flag zero-length and suspiciously small files (< 20 MB for movies/tv episodes, < 1 MB for youtube). Also list leftover junk: .part/.!qB/.tmp/.nzb/.par2/sample files, empty directories, and directories under movies/tv with no video file.
2. Header/container check with ffprobe on EVERY video file (this only reads headers, it's cheap): `ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration,size,bit_rate:stream=index,codec_type,codec_name -of json FILE`. Record: exit code, stderr (errors like "moov atom not found", "Invalid data found", "EBML header parsing failed"), duration, whether there is at least one video and one audio stream. Run with about 4-way parallelism (xargs -P4) inside the jellyfin container; write results as JSONL in the scratchpad. Files where ffprobe fails, or duration is missing/0, or no video/audio stream → BROKEN candidates.
3. Truncation check for MKV/MP4: a truncated download usually still has a valid header but a duration much shorter than expected, or an MKV without a Cues/duration element. Compare ffprobe duration against the expected runtime: Radarr `GET /api/v3/movie` → `runtime` (minutes) per movie (match by path), Sonarr `GET /api/v3/series` → `runtime` per series and `GET /api/v3/episodefile?seriesId=` → `mediaInfo.runTime`. Flag files whose duration is < 70% of the expected runtime (allow for specials/shorts; report the ratio). For files with no expected runtime, flag durations under 5 minutes in movies/tv.
4. Tail check for the BROKEN/truncated candidates only (not everything): `ffprobe -v error -read_intervals "99%" -show_entries frame=pkt_pts_time -of csv FILE 2>&1 | tail -3` or `ffmpeg -v error -sseek near end -t 10 -i FILE -f null -` limited to the last ~20 seconds, to confirm whether the file end is readable. Keep this to the candidate list.
5. Consistency with Radarr/Sonarr: movies: files on disk not referenced by any Radarr movieFile (orphans) and Radarr movieFiles whose path does not exist; TV: same via Sonarr episodefile paths; also Sonarr episodes with `hasFile: true` whose file is missing and series/episodes marked missing in Sonarr that are wanted (specifically "Sterling Point": list its episodes, hasFile, monitored, and any episodeFile entries and their mediaInfo). YouTube: report counts per channel folder, files with no matching .info.json/.nfo/.jpg sidecar if Pinchflat writes them, and any ffprobe failures.
6. Check Sonarr/Radarr history for past "import failed"/"corrupt"/"unable to parse mediainfo" events: `GET /api/v3/history?page=1&pageSize=200&eventType=...` or filter on `data.message` containing "corrupt", "MediaInfo", "failed" over the last 90 days; and both apps' `GET /api/v3/health` warnings.

REPORT (final message only): totals (files, size per folder); BROKEN list (path | size | ffprobe error | duration vs expected | Radarr/Sonarr id); TRUNCATED/short list; zero-length/junk/empty-dir list; orphans and missing-file lists (counts + first 20, full lists in scratchpad files, state paths); Sterling Point status; history/health findings; and any observation about how the corrupt files got there (e.g. failed usenet repair, partial imports). Do not delete anything.

## Jellyfin Metadata Audit — Read-Only

**Jellyfin version:** 10.11.11. No writes, deletes, moves, or restarts were performed.

### 1. Libraries

| Library | CollectionType | Path | Fetchers (order) | Key options |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Movies | movies | `/data/media/movies` | TheMovieDb → OMDb; images: TheMovieDb, OMDb, Embedded, Screen Grab | **EnableInternetProviders: false**, SaveLocalMetadata: false, RealtimeMonitor: true, lang: en, LocalMetadataReaderOrder: [Nfo] |
| TV | tvshows | `/data/media/tv` | Series/Episode: TheMovieDb → OMDb; Season: TheMovieDb | **EnableInternetProviders: false**, SaveLocalMetadata: false, RealtimeMonitor: true, lang: en |
| YouTube | tvshows | `/data/media/youtube/shows` | Series/Episode: TheMovieDb → OMDb | **EnableInternetProviders: false**, SaveLocalMetadata: false, RealtimeMonitor: true, lang: (blank) |
| Music | music | `/data/music` | MusicBrainz/TheAudioDB + "Neptune"/IMVDb plugins | EnableInternetProviders: false, RealtimeMonitor: false |

**Root cause found (applies almost everywhere below):** `EnableInternetProviders` is **false on every library**, and NFO writing is **disabled in both Radarr and Sonarr** (all Kodi/Emby-metadata connectors show `"enable": false`; Radarr `importExtraFiles: false`). No `.nfo` file exists anywhere under `/data/media/tv` or `/data/media/movies` (confirmed via `find`). Only the YouTube library gets NFOs — from Pinchflat, not Sonarr. Net effect: Jellyfin cannot fetch or re-fetch metadata for Movies/TV at all; it is running purely on whatever got matched/cached in the past. Anything added since internet providers were switched off comes in completely unidentified, and anything that was mis-matched while providers were on is now frozen wrong forever (auto-scans can't correct it).

### 2. Movies (167 items, 167 Radarr files, all paths exist — no orphans, no duplicate folders/Tmdb ids)

| ItemId | Name/Year/Tmdb (Jellyfin) | Folder | Folder Tmdb | Problem |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `26001c2c7186afa1fd410dac9bdb4283` | "The Imaginary Doctor" (2022), Tmdb **764393** | The Imaginary (2023) | **913001** | Wrong film entirely — matched to an unrelated title, not the Studio Ponoc film "The Imaginary" in the folder |
| `e354f3757803b0db1f6080e3abd49e5f` | "The Jungle Book" (1967), Tmdb **9325** | The Jungle Book (2016) | **278927** | Classic case named in the brief — matched to the 1967 cartoon instead of the 2016 live-action film |
| `ca53667ea3fb8c9add805b5834840352` | Name literally `"Ratatouille (2007) {tmdb-2062}"`, Year **2062**, no ProviderIds, no Overview | Ratatouille (2007) | 2062 | Fully unidentified — Jellyfin fell back to the raw folder string as title/year; needs Tmdb id set (correct id is 2062, but it never got applied to ProviderIds) |
| `9c675a476fd45d0b7f0caadbfa5f29cf` | "Scarlet" (2025), Tmdb **1484877** | Scarlet (2025) | **1406657** | Tmdb mismatch — folder and Jellyfin disagree on which "Scarlet (2025)" this is |

No missing posters/images found. Full issue list (4 records): `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/d3f24245-e5fb-4811-8dbe-b9304620c838/scratchpad/jf_movies_issues.json`

**Fix fields needed:** for each, `ItemId` + correct `ProviderIds.Tmdb` (from the folder's `{tmdb-XXXX}`), then re-identify/refresh metadata (Overview/Year/Images follow from the correct Tmdb id).

### 3. TV — Series (87 series total: 68 in `/data/media/tv`, 19 YouTube channels)

**TV library (68 series):** zero identification mismatches — every folder `{tvdb-XXXX}` agrees with Jellyfin's `Tvdb` provider id, no duplicates, no unidentified series, no missing series (Sonarr has 68 series with files, all 68 present in Jellyfin at matching paths).

**Sterling Point specifically (asked in the brief):** healthy. `ItemId cadbbe016e81aa6bab9c84835d900fbf`, folder `Sterling Point (2026) {tvdb-459552}` matches Jellyfin `Tvdb=459552`/`Tmdb=283297`/`Imdb=tt35618070` exactly. Sonarr (seriesId 326) shows 8/8 episode files monitored+downloaded for season 1; **episode 2 ("She's Giving Single & Bi") is present on disk, in Sonarr, and correctly indexed in Jellyfin as S01E02**. No problem here.

**YouTube channels (19, CollectionType tvshows):** because `EnableInternetProviders=false`, these should just carry the Pinchflat `youtube` NFO uniqueid — but **6 of the 19 channels somehow carry Tmdb/Tvdb/Imdb ids** (a leftover from when internet matching was presumably on), and three are confirmed wrong via TMDB/IMDb lookup:
- **"Boundary"** (dev-tools YouTube channel `@boundaryml`) → Tvdb 272697 / Tmdb 61695 = **"Beyond the Boundary"**, an unrelated 2013 anime. Wrong match.
- **"NPR Music"** → Tmdb 70558 = **"NPR Tiny Desk Concerts"**, a narrower/different show than the full NPR Music channel. Likely wrong/too-narrow match.
- **"New Money"** (finance channel) → Imdb tt4759938 = a 2015 reality-TV series "New Money" about nouveau-riche families. Wrong match.
- **"DanTDM"** → Tmdb 77329 = "DanTDM Creates a Big Scene" (a real but narrow official miniseries, not the general channel) — borderline, worth reviewing.
- **"Patrick Boyle"** → Imdb tt15661346 only (no Tmdb/Tvdb) — could not verify target via available web tools (IMDb blocked fetch attempts); flag for manual check.
- The other 13 channels have no ProviderIds at all (correctly unidentified given the config, not misidentified).

Series-level issue list (16 records): `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/d3f24245-e5fb-4811-8dbe-b9304620c838/scratchpad/jf_series_issues.json`

**Fix:** clear the wrong `ProviderIds` (Boundary, New Money, NPR Music, and review DanTDM/Patrick Boyle) so they fall back to the Pinchflat NFO's `youtube` id only, and turn `EnableInternetProviders` off consistently (it already is) so nothing re-matches to TVDB/TMDB by title text again.

### 4. TV — Episodes (1520 real TV episodes; 0 with S/E-number-vs-filename mismatches; 0 virtual/missing placeholders — Jellyfin only ever shows episodes that have files)

Two real data-integrity problems surfaced by comparing Sonarr episode-file counts to Jellyfin episode counts:

- **"The Summer Hikaru Died"** (`tvdb-450428`): Sonarr counts 12 episode files; Jellyfin shows only 1 item. Cause: all 12 episodes were released/packaged as **one single video file** named `S01E01-E12`, so Jellyfin (correctly) creates one merged episode item rather than 12 — not a bug, but worth knowing individual-episode jump/resume won't work.
- **"The Powerpuff Girls"** (`tvdb-76200`), Season 6: Sonarr counts 27 episode files; Jellyfin shows 15 items (multi-episode files merged 2:1, as expected) — **but the episode titles are wrong for most of them**. Confirmed by direct comparison of filename-embedded titles vs Jellyfin's stored `Name`:
  - Jellyfin E1 ("S06E01-E02") shows title **"Little Miss Interprets / Night Mayor"** — that title actually belongs to the S06E10-E11 file. Every title from E1 through E17 is shifted from its real content.
  - Jellyfin E19, E20, E22, E24, E26 (5 items) have **no title at all** — `Name` just falls back to the series name "The Powerpuff Girls".
  - This is a genuine, confirmed metadata mismatch: `ItemId`s for the 15 episode entries under SeriesId `dd49d88fa730f39f52320f69b08a9ab5`, needs episode metadata refresh/re-identify per item once a real metadata source is restored (see root cause above — currently there is none).

**Missing episode-title metadata (not wrong, just empty), a symptom of the same root cause:** 164 TV episodes have `Name == SeriesName` (i.e., no title at all) — 156 of these are **all of "One Piece" seasons 12–13** (100% of those two seasons), plus 5 in Powerpuff Girls S6 (above), 1 each in The Bear/The Hawk/Unicorn Academy. A further 44 episodes show Jellyfin's generic `"Episode N"` placeholder: Violet Evergarden (13), Agent Kim Reactivated (10), MasterChef Australia (9), Mind Over Murder (6), House of the Dragon (4), 2 others. Full detail: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mm-dev-home-infra/d3f24245-e5fb-4811-8dbe-b9304620c838/scratchpad/jf_title_mismatches.json` (also contains ~150 further "low text-similarity" hits between filename and Jellyfin title that are almost all false positives — dub-title vs literal-release-title differences for anime like Yu-Gi-Oh!/One Piece, not real mismatches; only the Powerpuff Girls case above was independently confirmed as a genuine wrong-title bug).

**Fix fields needed:** restore a metadata source (enable Sonarr's Kodi/Emby NFO export, or turn `EnableInternetProviders` back on for TV), then trigger a metadata refresh on: One Piece (SeriesId `dcda80f8ce91daea0c0ccb81f74b7ef0`), Powerpuff Girls (`dd49d88fa730f39f52320f69b08a9ab5`), Violet Evergarden, Agent Kim Reactivated, MasterChef Australia, Mind Over Murder, House of the Dragon.

cd /Users/mm/dev/home-infra-media && cat > docs/media-metadata.md <<'EOF'
# Media metadata and library integrity

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

How Radarr, Sonarr, Jellyfin and Plex agree on what a file is, and how broken
files are caught. These settings live in the applications (Docker volumes),
not in Git, so this page is the record of the intended state.

## Identity flows from the download managers

- Radarr and Sonarr name folders with the provider id (`{tmdb-…}` for movies,
  `{tvdb-…}` for series) and write Kodi/Emby NFO sidecars with the same ids
  (Settings → Metadata → Kodi (XBMC) / Emby, metadata on, images off). The
  media servers read those ids instead of guessing from titles, which is what
  produced "The Jungle Book (2016)" matched to the 1967 cartoon.
- Both apps have Connect notifications to Plex and Jellyfin with "Update
  Library" on for import, upgrade, rename and delete, so the affected folder is
  rescanned immediately. NFS does not deliver inotify events, so this is the
  primary trigger; Plex additionally runs a scheduled scan every six hours.

## Jellyfin

| Library | Type | Path | Metadata |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Movies | movies | `/data/media/movies` | NFO first, then TheMovieDb and OMDb (internet providers on) |
| TV | tvshows | `/data/media/tv` | NFO first, then TheTVDB, TheMovieDb, OMDb (internet providers on) |
| YouTube | tvshows | `/data/media/youtube/shows` | NFO only (internet providers off) |
| Music | music | `/data/music` | MusicBrainz and TheAudioDB |

Internet providers must stay off for YouTube: Pinchflat writes `tvshow.nfo`
and per-video NFOs with a `youtube` unique id, and any online provider will
match a channel name to an unrelated TV series (Boundary became the anime
"Beyond the Boundary"). Channel items must carry only the `youtube` id.

The TheTVDB plugin is installed because TheMovieDb has no episode titles for
several series (One Piece, talk shows). When titles are missing after a
provider change, refresh the series with "Replace all metadata"; a plain
refresh keeps the existing placeholder name.

## Plex

| Section | Type | Agent | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Movies | movie | Plex Movie | honours `{tmdb-…}` in folder names |
| TV | show | Plex TV Series | aired order |
| YouTube | show (hidden) | Plex NFO Series | one show per channel folder, seasons flattened |
| Music | artist (hidden) | Plex Music | |

The YouTube section must use the NFO agent. With the online TV agent every
channel's videos were pooled into one show because Pinchflat's date-based
episode numbers collide across channels. Changing the agent on an existing
section does not split the pooled show; the section had to be deleted and
re-created (watched state comes back from Jellyfin via jellyplex-watched).

Unmatched movies (`local://` guid) are usually new imports the agent has not
matched yet; "Refresh metadata" on the item matches it from the folder id.

## File integrity

Radarr and Sonarr validate only container headers on import. A 3 GB episode
with Matroska structural errors scattered through its body imported cleanly
and only failed a full demux pass:

```console
ffmpeg -v error -i FILE -c copy -f null -
```

The `checkrr` stack (see [docs/checkrr.md](checkrr.md)) runs that class of
check on new files and hands corrupt ones back to Radarr or Sonarr for
re-download. To fix one by hand: delete the episode or movie file in the app,
mark the grab as failed in History (this blocklists the release) and search
again, then re-run the demux check on the replacement.

## Jellyfin container mounts

Music is mounted once, at `/data/music`, which is the library path. An
earlier duplicate mount of `/mnt/music` at `/data/media/music` was nested
inside the read-only media bind and depended on an empty `music/` directory
existing on the NFS share; when that directory disappeared the container could
not start after a restart. Keep nested bind mounts out of read-only binds.
EOF

----
---
services:
  checkrr:
    image: aetaric/checkrr:3.6.1@sha256:c817e081e9397c240e5b13b09363fe26c9f94248489d3b4f0279e67495b1f12e
    container_name: checkrr
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    # Upstream's alpine-based image has no non-root user baked in (unlike
    # Recyclarr's fixed 1000:1000 user), so this runs as root. cap_drop ALL,
    # no-new-privileges, and a read-only root filesystem contain it; the only
    # writable paths are the checkrr-data volume and the /tmp tmpfs, and the
    # media library is bind-mounted read-only below. See docs/checkrr.md.
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp
    networks:
      - proxy
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ}
      - RADARR_API_KEY=${RADARR_API_KEY}
      - SONARR_API_KEY=${SONARR_API_KEY}
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/config/entrypoint.sh"]
    volumes:
      - checkrr-data:/data
      - ./checkrr.yaml.tpl:/config/checkrr.yaml.tpl:ro
      - ./entrypoint.sh:/config/entrypoint.sh:ro
      - type: bind
        source: /mnt/data/media
        target: /data/media
        read_only: true
        bind:
          propagation: rslave
    # Checkrr walks its configured paths sequentially with no worker pool, so
    # only one file is ever being demuxed/decoded at a time regardless of
    # these limits. They exist to cap ffmpeg's CPU/RAM use during a full
    # decode pass so the 6-core/8GB docker-host VM and the NFS-backed media
    # library aren't starved by a long-running scan; cpu_shares gives every
    # other container priority over it under contention.
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2.0"
          memory: 1g
    cpu_shares: 512
    # No healthcheck: this is a cron-scheduled batch job with no listening
    # port (the optional web UI is not enabled) and the image ships no
    # health-check script, matching the recyclarr stack's rationale.
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  checkrr-data:
    name: checkrr-data

networks:
  proxy:
    external: true
----
# Checkrr configuration template. See docs/checkrr.md for how this is
# deployed, how secrets are injected, and how to run a one-off scan.
#
# The __RADARR_API_KEY__ / __SONARR_API_KEY__ placeholders are substituted by
# entrypoint.sh from the RADARR_API_KEY / SONARR_API_KEY environment
# variables at container start; the rendered file only ever exists in the

The Bluray copy of Beauty and the Beast is downloading with a watcher on it, and that's the last open item on the media side. Here is where everything stands, plus one question.

**Fixed today**

- Jellyfin: internet metadata providers enabled for Movies and TV, TheTVDB plugin installed and made the primary TV source, four mis-identified movies corrected (Jungle Book 2016, The Imaginary, Ratatouille, Scarlet), five YouTube channels stripped of bogus TV-show ids, all missing episode titles resolved (the remaining "Episode N" names are TheTVDB's real titles).
- Plex: seven unmatched movies matched, four stale file references fixed, Star Wars: Visions S2 episodes matched, periodic scans enabled every six hours, YouTube library rebuilt with the NFO agent: 12 channels, 286 of 286 videos, no merged episodes.
- Radarr and Sonarr now write NFO sidecars with TMDB and TVDB ids for every file, so both servers identify from the id rather than the title.
- Sterling Point S01E02: the corruption was in the FLUX release itself. Both indexer copies are blocklisted and a playWEB copy passes a full demux check, indexed in both servers.
- Remux downgrade: library is 1,253 GB, down from 1,788 GB. Remaining Remuxes are Coraline (no WEB release exists) and two dual-audio anime titles kept deliberately.

**One incident, resolved.** My Jellyfin restart exposed a fragile compose mount: a duplicate music bind nested inside the read-only media bind needed an empty directory on the NFS share that no longer existed, so the container couldn't start. I recreated the directory and Jellyfin was down for about six minutes. The redundant mount is removed in the pending change.

**Your call on the PR.** You denied the step that would move the Checkrr files out of your working tree. Right now the Checkrr stack (`docker/checkrr/`, `docs/checkrr.md`, README and stack-list edits) sits uncommitted on your `fix-cg13` checkout, and a separate worktree at `../home-infra-media` holds the media-metadata doc, the Jellyfin compose fix and its README link. input.command:
cp docker/checkrr/checkrr.yaml.tpl ../home-infra-media/docker/recyclarr/checkrr.yaml.tpl && cp docker/checkrr/entrypoint.sh ../home-infra-media/docker/recyclarr/checkrr-entrypoint.sh && cp docs/checkrr.md ../home-infra-media/docs/checkrr.md && cd ../home-infra-media && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
# 1. compose: add checkrr service + volume to the recyclarr stack
p='docker/recyclarr/compose.yml'; s=open(p).read()
svc='''
  checkrr:
    image: aetaric/checkrr:3.6.1@sha256:c817e081e9397c240e5b13b09363fe26c9f94248489d3b4f0279e67495b1f12e
    container_name: checkrr
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    # Upstream's image has no non-root user, so this runs as root; cap_drop
    # ALL, no-new-privileges and a read-only root filesystem contain it. The
    # only writable paths are the checkrr-data volume and the /tmp tmpfs; the
    # media library is bind-mounted read-only. See docs/checkrr.md.
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp
    networks:
      - proxy
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ}
      - RADARR_API_KEY=${RADARR_API_KEY}
      - SONARR_API_KEY=${SONARR_API_KEY}
    # Checkrr has no env-var config support, so the entrypoint renders the
    # template with the API keys into tmpfs at start (docs/checkrr.md).
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "/config/entrypoint.sh"]
    volumes:
      - checkrr-data:/data
      - ./checkrr.yaml.tpl:/config/checkrr.yaml.tpl:ro
      - ./checkrr-entrypoint.sh:/config/entrypoint.sh:ro
      - type: bind
        source: /mnt/data/media
        target: /data/media
        read_only: true
        bind:
          propagation: rslave
    # Checkrr checks one file at a time; these limits cap ffmpeg's CPU/RAM
    # during a full decode pass so other containers and the NFS server are
    # not starved, and cpu_shares yields to every other container.
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2.0"
          memory: 1g
    cpu_shares: 512
    # No healthcheck: cron-scheduled batch job with no listening port.
    restart: unless-stopped
'''
s=s.replace("\nvolumes:\n  recyclarr-data:\n    name: recyclarr-data\n", svc+"\nvolumes:\n  recyclarr-data:\n    name: recyclarr-data\n  checkrr-data:\n    name: checkrr-data\n")
assert 'checkrr-data' in s; open(p,'w').write(s)
# 2. README table row + intro sentence
p='README.md'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("| **recyclarr**        | Recyclarr (TRaSH sync for Radarr and Sonarr)   |","| **recyclarr**        | Recyclarr (TRaSH sync), Checkrr (integrity)    |")
s=s.replace("[docs/recyclarr.md](docs/recyclarr.md). Library identity, metadata provider\nsettings and file-integrity checking are described in\n[docs/media-metadata.md](docs/media-metadata.md).",
 "[docs/recyclarr.md](docs/recyclarr.md); the same stack runs Checkrr, which scans\nfor corrupt files and re-downloads them via Radarr/Sonarr\n([docs/checkrr.md](docs/checkrr.md)). Library identity and metadata provider\nsettings are described in [docs/media-metadata.md](docs/media-metadata.md).")
open(p,'w').write(s)
# 3. docs/checkrr.md deployment section -> shares the recyclarr stack
p='docs/checkrr.md'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('docker/checkrr/checkrr.yaml.tpl','docker/recyclarr/checkrr.yaml.tpl').replace('docker/checkrr/entrypoint.sh','docker/recyclarr/checkrr-entrypoint.sh').replace('docker/checkrr/compose.yml','docker/recyclarr/compose.yml').replace('`checkrr` Portainer stack','`recyclarr` Portainer stack').replace('`checkrr` stack','`recyclarr` stack')
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('worktree assembled')
EOF
